```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(rvest); library(robotstxt); library(tidyverse); library(tidytext)
library(textrank); library(lexRankr); library(wordcloud); library(RColorBrewer)
library(igraph); library(ggraph); library(textstem)

```

# Question 3.1 - Fair-use web scraping into an R data structure

**Website chosen:** Wikipedia article *"Big data"*. Wikipedia text is published under the
Creative Commons BY-SA licence. The page's `robots.txt` permission is verified before scraping,
a delay is applied after the request and only one page is requested, in line with fair use of web scraping.

```{r scrape}
# Q3.1
url <- "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_data"
allowed <- paths_allowed(url)
cat("Scraping allowed by robots.txt:", allowed, "\n")
stopifnot(allowed)

page <- read_html(url); Sys.sleep(2)
xml2::xml_remove(html_elements(page, "style, script, sup.reference, .mw-editsection"))
paras <- page |> html_elements("#mw-content-text .mw-parser-output > p") |> html_text2()
if (length(paras) < 5) paras <- page |> html_elements("#mw-content-text p") |> html_text2()
if (length(paras) < 5) paras <- page |> html_elements("p") |> html_text2()
cat("Paragraphs scraped:", length(paras), "\n")
stopifnot(length(paras) >= 5)

web_df <- tibble(para_id = seq_along(paras), text = paras) |>
  filter(str_trim(text) != "")
str(web_df)
head(web_df |> mutate(text = substr(text, 1, 150)), 5)
```

# Question 3.2 - Text preprocessing

The following preprocessing techniques were applied: removal of citation markers such as `[12]` and
`[citation needed]`, removal of bracketed asides, transliteration and removal of non-ASCII characters,
whitespace normalisation, removal of very short paragraphs, sentence segmentation, word tokenisation,
stop-word and number removal, removal of short tokens and lemmatisation.

```{r preprocess}
# Q3.2
web_df <- web_df |>
  mutate(text = text |>
           str_remove_all("\\[(\\d+|citation needed|[a-z]|note \\d+)\\]") |>
           str_remove_all("\\.?mw-parser-output[^}]*\\}") |>
           str_replace_all("\\([^)]*\\)", " ") |>
           stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>
           str_replace_all("[^ -~]", " ") |>
           str_squish()) |>
  filter(nchar(text) > 40)

sentences <- web_df |>
  mutate(sentence = tokenizers::tokenize_sentences(text)) |>
  select(para_id, sentence) |>
  tidyr::unnest(sentence) |>
  mutate(sentence = str_squish(sentence)) |>
  filter(nchar(sentence) > 30) |>
  mutate(textrank_id = row_number())

words <- sentences |>
  tidytext::unnest_tokens(output = word, input = sentence) |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  filter(!str_detect(word, "\\d"), nchar(word) > 2) |>
  mutate(word = if_else(word == "data", word, lemmatize_words(word)))

cat("Paragraphs:", nrow(web_df), "| Sentences:", nrow(sentences), "| Clean tokens:", nrow(words), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(sentences) > 5)
head(sentences, 5)
```

# Question 3.3 - Text summarisation

## Technique 1 - TextRank (graph-based extractive summary)

Each sentence is a node in a graph, edges are weighted by the words two sentences share, and the
PageRank algorithm selects the most central sentences.

```{r textrank}
# Q3.3
tr <- textrank_sentences(data = sentences |> select(textrank_id, sentence),
                         terminology = words |> select(textrank_id, word))
textrank_summary <- summary(tr, n = 5, keep.sentence.order = TRUE)
cat(paste0("- ", textrank_summary), sep = "\n")
```

## Technique 2 - Frequency-based (Luhn) summary

Each sentence is scored by the average normalised frequency of its important words.

```{r luhn}
# Q3.3
freq <- words |> count(word, sort = TRUE) |> mutate(w = n / max(n))
luhn <- words |> inner_join(freq, by = "word") |>
  group_by(textrank_id) |> summarise(score = sum(w) / n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(sentences, by = "textrank_id")
luhn_summary <- luhn |> slice_max(score, n = 5) |> arrange(textrank_id)
cat(paste0("- ", luhn_summary$sentence), sep = "\n")
```

## Technique 3 - LexRank (cosine-similarity graph)

```{r lexrank}
# Q3.3
lex <- lexRank(sentences$sentence, n = 5, continuous = TRUE, Verbose = FALSE)
cat(paste0("- ", lex$sentence), sep = "\n")
```

## Visualisation 1 - Most frequent terms

```{r vis1}
# Q3.3
freq |> slice_max(n, n = 15) |>
  ggplot(aes(reorder(word, n), n)) + geom_col(fill = "darkcyan") + coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 15 Terms in the Wikipedia 'Big data' Article",
       x = "Term (lemmatised)", y = "Frequency")
```

## Visualisation 2 - Word cloud

```{r vis2, fig.height=7}
# Q3.3
wordcloud(freq$word, freq$n, max.words = 80, random.order = FALSE, colors = brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"))
title("Word Cloud of the 'Big data' Article")
```

## Visualisation 3 - Sentence importance (TextRank) across the article

```{r vis3}
# Q3.3
tr$sentences |>
  ggplot(aes(textrank_id, textrank)) + geom_line(colour = "grey40") + geom_point(colour = "red") +
  labs(title = "TextRank Score of Each Sentence", x = "Sentence number (order in article)",
       y = "TextRank importance score")
```

## Visualisation 4 - Bigram network

```{r vis4, fig.height=8}
# Q3.3
bigrams <- tibble(bigram = unlist(tokenizers::tokenize_ngrams(web_df$text, n = 2))) |>
  filter(!is.na(bigram)) |>
  separate(bigram, c("w1", "w2"), sep = " ") |>
  filter(!w1 %in% stop_words$word, !w2 %in% stop_words$word,
         !str_detect(w1, "\\d"), !str_detect(w2, "\\d")) |>
  count(w1, w2, sort = TRUE) |> filter(n >= 2)

graph_from_data_frame(head(bigrams, 50)) |>
  ggraph(layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(aes(width = n), alpha = 0.4, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_node_point(colour = "orange", size = 3) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE, size = 3.5) +
  scale_edge_width(range = c(0.5, 3), name = "Bigram count") +
  labs(title = "Bigram Network of the 'Big data' Article") + theme_void()
```

# Findings

```{r findings3, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
tr_ids  <- tr$sentences |> filter(sentence %in% textrank_summary) |> pull(textrank_id)
lex_ids <- sentences$textrank_id[match(lex$sentence, sentences$sentence)]
ov_tl <- length(intersect(tr_ids, luhn_summary$textrank_id))
ov_tx <- length(intersect(tr_ids, lex_ids))
ov_lx <- length(intersect(luhn_summary$textrank_id, lex_ids))
top_sent <- tr$sentences |> slice_max(textrank, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
top5 <- head(freq, 5)
bg <- head(bigrams, 5)
pos <- if (top_sent$textrank_id <= nrow(sentences) / 3) "the opening part" else if (top_sent$textrank_id <= 2 * nrow(sentences) / 3) "the middle" else "the final part"

cat(sprintf("The web page was converted into an R data frame of %d paragraphs, which after preprocessing produced %d sentences and %d clean word tokens for analysis.\n\n",
            nrow(web_df), nrow(sentences), nrow(words)))
cat(sprintf("**TextRank** selected five sentences that together describe what big data is, its characteristics and how it is used. The single most central sentence (number %d, located in %s of the article) is: *\"%s\"*\n\n",
            top_sent$textrank_id, pos, top_sent$sentence))
cat(sprintf("**Comparison of techniques:** TextRank and the frequency-based (Luhn) summary share %d of their five sentences, TextRank and LexRank share %d, and Luhn and LexRank share %d. ",
            ov_tl, ov_tx, ov_lx),
    "The graph-based methods (TextRank and LexRank) favour sentences that are similar to many other sentences and therefore capture the overall theme of the article, while the frequency-based method favours sentences that are dense in the most repeated terms and tends to be more specific.\n\n")
cat(sprintf("**Term frequency and word cloud:** the dominant terms are *%s*. Their prominence confirms that the article focuses on the nature of data, its analysis and the technologies used to process it.\n\n",
            paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", top5$word, top5$n), collapse = ", ")))
cat(sprintf("**Sentence importance:** TextRank scores range from %.4f to %.4f across the article, so a small number of sentences carry most of the article's central meaning.\n\n",
            min(tr$sentences$textrank), max(tr$sentences$textrank)))
if (nrow(bg) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("**Bigram network:** the most frequent word pairs are *%s*. These pairs form the main clusters in the network and highlight the key concepts the article links together.\n",
              paste(sprintf("%s %s (%d)", bg$w1, bg$w2, bg$n), collapse = ", ")))
}
```
